theorist: C: Asta Theorizer (gpt-5.2 / gpt-5-mini, literature-grounded) mapped by a tool-less Claude Sonnet call (claude -p --tools '', 1 turn)

H1.theory: Stiffness-contrast scattering from SiC inclusions is missing in mass-only models, so chemistry-aware MD would give a larger reduction than the continuum bracket.
H1.falsifier: MD at R=2.0 nm giving a reduction inside 40-75 %
H1.reach: Mass-only models would then be adequate for SiC inclusions.
H1.basis: If a SiGe nanocomposite contains chemistry-distinct inclusions (e.g., SiC) rather than isomorphous Si/Ge inclusions, then a mass-only inclusion model will systematically underpredict the inclusion’s κ suppression relative to chemistry-aware (DFT/ML) models because stiffness/topology scattering is missing.

H2.theory: Finite-size and potential-dispersion errors are amplified near the end members where intrinsic scattering is weak, so the fitted law breaks down there and the high points are physical.
H2.falsifier: High-x points disappearing when box size is increased and the Tersoff dispersion is checked
H2.reach: Low-order empirical laws would not be trusted near the end members.
H2.basis: Fitted low-order empirical laws for kappa(x,T) derived from finite-size MD boxes will show composition-dependent breakdown near end members more readily than DFT-BTE/VCA curves, because finite-size and potential-dispersion errors are amplified when intrinsic scattering is weak (near pure Si or pure Ge).

H4.theory: Amorphous kappa has weaker length dependence than the crystal, and any residual dependence is kappa rising with length as low-frequency modes are better represented.
H4.falsifier: kappa falling with cell length after statistical convergence
H4.reach: Amorphous kappa from small boxes would be underconverged.
H4.basis: Reverse-NEMD (or EMD) κ for amorphous Si0.5Ge0.5 will show substantially weaker length dependence than crystalline Si0.5Ge0.5 in comparable cell geometries; any residual length dependence should primarily appear as κ increasing with length as the low-frequency sector becomes better represented.

H8.theory: Perfect-crystal DFT-BTE is an upper envelope and real microstructure such as grain boundaries lowers kappa further.
H8.reach: almaBTE would be a ceiling rather than a calibrated prediction for sintered samples.
H8.basis: Perfect-crystal calculations give the high end. Real microstructures usually lower κ, and they do so more when grains/interfaces are small enough to block the long-traveling phonons.

H9.theory: A thin oxide cap removes the free surface as a Sn sink and so suppresses the change. The uncapped film shows an incubation of about 50 min before collapse.
H9.falsifier: Capped and uncapped films showing the same incubation and collapse at 550 °C
H9.reach: The surface sink would not control the Sn loss.
H9.basis: Uncapped SiGeSn at 550 °C shows ~50 min incubation then rapid collapse with a fitted logistic width of ~1.9 min; 3 nm SiO2-capped Si0.08Ge0.88Sn0.04 shows <1 at.% Sn change over 140 min at 550 °C, |ΔE2| < 20 meV, no voids, preserved uniform Sn (EDX/APT), limited strain relaxation, and far lower contact resistivity than uncapped.

O1.theory: VSnV formation becomes more favourable and binding strengthens with Sn content, so Sn adjacent to a vacancy is bound at 12 % Sn, probably by more than 0.3 eV.
O1.falsifier: MACE-MP-0 giving negative Sn-vacancy binding in Ge0.88Sn0.12
O1.reach: The complexation-controlled low-barrier regime would be undermined.
O1.basis: O1 (Ge0.88Sn0.12, MACE-MP-0 static): a substitutional Sn adjacent to a vacancy is predicted to be bound (positive binding). Category-level expectation: 'bound by 0 to 0.3 eV' or 'bound by more than 0.3 eV' (leaning >0.3 eV given VSnV stabilization trends at higher Sn, but noting dopant-free context matters).

O2.theory: Vacancy-assisted Sn hops show a low-barrier effective activation energy, well below bulk Ge and in the metastable-film range.
O2.category: close to the low-temperature metastable-film value (1.1 to 1.8 eV)
O2.falsifier: MD hop activation energies of 2.9-3.3 eV
O2.reach: Low-temperature enhanced Sn diffusion would be attributed to vacancy complexation.
O2.basis: O2 (Ge0.88Sn0.12 with vacancies, 500–700 K MD): effective activation energy for observed Sn hops is predicted to be well below bulk Ge substitutional diffusion (2.9–3.3 eV) and more consistent with a low-barrier regime (category: 'close to the low-temperature metastable-film value (1.1 to 1.8 eV)' rather than bulk-like).
